done.why: On my third death the game ended for good. I'd respawned at the Endless Stair, forgot to pick up the lantern, walked south into the dark and a grue ate me. The old man's voice said goodnight and left me in the Void, and after that nothing I typed did anything.

about: An old man waits at the bottom of the dungeon to see if you're worthy. He's pictured wearing a hood, cloak, amulet and ring, carrying a book, staff and key, so the job is to collect those, plus whatever you need on the way, and earn the way down the secret stair. Mostly it's about earning things: a thief who keeps his word, a sailor waiting for the right greeting, a hungry old man, and a cold lake that takes everything you carry.

ending.what: A losing ending. After my third death the old man's voice says he's waited for me but maybe it was someone else he wanted, and leaves me in the Void with the game over. I never got down the secret stair.

moments.note: Tying the chest to the rope just worked, and a figure moving at the top of the cliff told me something was coming.
Waiting on the ledge, the same text about the lock being tried came back three times. I couldn't tell if I was supposed to keep waiting.
The thief came back like he said and gave me the staff. Waiting turned out to be the right call.
'hello, sailor' worked and the sailor threw me a vial.
Gave the old man the bread and he showed me a secret door. Felt like real progress.
The secret stair turned me back, but it told me plainly that nothing here was left undone and what I needed was in places I hadn't been yet. Useful.
Went into the lake and dropped everything I had, staff and vial included. There was a warning, but I took it to mean light and swords.
Dived and got swallowed by a giant fish on the very first turn.
Every time I grabbed the shiny thing in the sand it slipped away. Never worked out how to get it.
The Southern Shore text basically told me grue repellent comes in a can, somewhere a light has already been. Good hint.
Touched the vista table and landed in a sacrificial temple, where I died straight away. Funny, harsh.
Took the torch and rode the table to the Timber Room. Felt like visiting an old place.
The vista showed a spray can in Room 8, and touching the table took me there to grab it. The hint paid off.
Sprayed myself and swam over, but the repellent had nearly worn off by the time I reached the grue lair.
Respawned and walked straight into the dark without the lantern. Game over for good. My own fault, but it hit hard.

wished: I wished I could carry the can across the lake some way other than my bare hands, or knew sooner that diving, grabbing things underwater and surfacing lets you carry them.
I wished I could pull the sword out of the rock. It said 'Who do you think you are? Arthur?' and later 'can't budge it', and never told me what would change that.
I wished I could get hold of the shiny object in the lake sand.
I wished I'd met whoever's footsteps were in the Land of Shadow.
I wished the third death had a warning before it, or that the respawn had put the lantern in my hands instead of at my feet.

lines.line: The door is open, and will stay open. The way down is not yours today. You come back up.
lines.why: It turned me away kindly and told me exactly what kind of thing was missing. That kept me going.

lines.line: He is dressed simply in a hood and cloak, wearing an amulet and ring, carrying an old book under one arm, and leaning on a wooden staff. A single key, as if to a massive prison cell, hangs from his belt.
lines.why: This turned the death into a shopping list. It's how I knew what the place wanted from me.

lines.line: what keeps a grue off a person is sold in a can, and the can is somewhere a light has already been.
lines.why: A riddle-ish hint that led me to the vista table and Room 8.

lines.line: the way a man paces who is deciding something, and deciding it in his own favour.
lines.why: Great description of the thief making up his mind. It made the waiting tense instead of empty.

lines.line: I have waited a long age for you, my friend, but perhaps it has been another that I have been seeking. Good night, oh worthy adventurer!
lines.why: The goodbye that ended my run. It stung, and it was well put.

fun.why: The puzzles I solved felt great: the chest and rope, hello sailor, the bread, getting the can through the vista. Losing my things in the lake twice and the sudden fish and temple deaths took some shine off.

engagement.why: Once the old man's description told me what to collect, I had a clear goal, and the hints kept pointing me forward. My attention only dropped while I waited on the ledge and walked the empty Land of Shadow.

difficulty.why: Only three deaths are allowed, and two came with almost no warning (the fish, the temple). The lake strips everything you carry, so getting the can over took timing I didn't manage. The third death was my own carelessness, but it ended the whole game.

interestingness.why: Being carried to other places by the vista table, and the thief who keeps his word in his own sly way, were both surprising. The lake had its own rules and felt alive.

prose.why: The added lines were really good: the man pacing 'deciding it in his own favour', the lake that 'would not give back what fell out of them', the turn-back on the stair. Clear and full of atmosphere.
